Q: Compare JSON Object with random List in Object A:

You have asked an experimental type of question meant to solicit opinions and discussion rather than a "correct" answer. But the question reads like a regular question for which there should be an objectively correct answer. What is your intent? To get an objectively correct answer? Or to get a variety of advice?

Q: Using Node.js, Ctrl + C doesn't the stop server (after starting the server with "npm start") A:

Inside package.json under scripts I had the line react-scripts start&.

Notice it ends with an & which would send the process to the background, and Ctrl + C will not work. Somehow trying to bring this to the foreground with fg also did not work.

I solved the problem by removing the &.

Q: Losing changes silently after rebase + Squash & Merge in team workflow A:

It is unclear what you mean by "When my coworker reviewed it, he noticed changes inside that function had disappeared."

  • Did they know exactly what changes you were going to show them for review, and they found that not all of the changes were in the commit?

  • Or did you undo someone else's changes (accidentally), and that is what they reported to you, and now you tell us this fact, but you use the words "changes disappeared" instead of calling it "I somehow reverted other people's changes"?

I am asking for clarification, because the way you describe your workflow does not show a mistake immediately, but there are potential pitfalls depending on the details of the case.

Q: How to call a stored procedure from a Spring Batch Tasklet? A:

Instead of

value="call stored_procedure()"

just put

value="stored_procedure"

without () on end. That should resolve your issue

Q: Sort execution failure in SAS A:

If you are working on z/OS, use "prco sql nothreads;"

If the SAS threaded sort is used, the host sort is not used. But the host sort is much better.

Q: Encoding PCM (CMSampleBufferRef) to AAC on iOS - How to set frequency and bitrate? A:

You may need to change the sample rate of the raw audio data by using a resampling audio unit before feeding the audio to the AAC converter. Otherwise there will be a mismatch between the AAC header and the audio data.

Q: Add variables to tuple A:

Tuples are immutable; you can't change which variables they contain after construction. However, you can concatenate or slice them to form new tuples:

a = (1, 2, 3,)
b = a + (4, 5, 6,)  # (1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6)
c = b[1:]  # (2, 3, 4, 5, 6)

And, of course, build them from existing values:

name = "Joe"
age = 40
location = "New York"
joe = (name, age, location)
